messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Automated alert: spike in CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS errors on us-west-2 serving-rt-3. 18 pods reporting; 3 nodes autocordoned; eviction rate up 40% in 5m. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving/cuda-illegal
incident-bot: Severity: P1 — please ack and triage.
alice: ack — I’m on it. @ravi are you oncall for runtime?
ravi: I am. jumping in now. any customer-facing impact metrics?
sam: Support looking — AcmeCorp and two other tenants reporting 5xxs and higher latency. Acme metric: 30% 5xx over last 10m.
marta: quick logs from one failing pod (runtime-rt-3-7f8):
```
[2026-03-17T16:02:14Z] runtime: ERROR: CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS at 0x7fbedc3f4b20
kernel: attention_kernel+0x4f
stack: gpu-sched -> serve_loop -> attention_kernel
notes: misaligned device pointer observed on memcpy from user space
```
ops-bot: node usw2-node-45 autocordoned (eviction threshold exceeded).
ops-bot: snapshotting /var/log/nvidia-crashdump -> s3://redwood-crashdumps/6234570001/
alice: thanks. @marta can you paste the container runtime stacktrace + coredump link?
marta: uploaded: https://s3.redwood/internal/crashes/6234570001/runtime-rt-3-7f8.core.gz

ravi: initial plan: 1) reduce concurrency on serving pods to 1 to limit parallel kernel launches 2) rollback recent kernel-level patch (deployed 2h ago) on canary nodes 3) enable model-variant fallback (v1-quant-safe) for high-traffic routes 4) collect nvcrash + nvprof traces for one repro pod.
alice: ok do the above. add mitigation tags to LB to shift 30% traffic to warm standby region (us-east-1) while we triage.
sam: drafting customer note for AcmeCorp — can we get ETA on mitigation?
ravi: ETA 20m for initial mitigation (concurrency + fallback) then 60m for full remediation if rollback repros the issue.
leah: sending a short message to AcmeCorp now: "We’re investigating a runtime GPU error affecting a subset of requests. Mitigations in progress. Will update in 20 minutes."
leah: sent.
marta: repro command I ran:
```
# reproduce load pattern
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/prod/generate -d '{"prompt":"<long_seq>","max_tokens":2048}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' &
# observed illegal access after ~120s under continuous KV-cache warmup
```

ops-bot: cordon scheduled for nodes with highest eviction count; draining blocked until rollback applied.

ravi: applying concurrency patch to deployment serving-rt-3: set env REDWOOD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 -> rolling restart. Applying model routing change to use v1-quant-safe for routes: /api/generate heavy and /api/chat heavy.
alice: while that rolls, enable CUDA memcheck on one repro pod to gather addresses: set env CUDA_MEMCHECK=1 for debug pod only. Note: memcheck has CPU overhead, keep to one pod.
marta: memcheck logs (attached) show misaligned memcpy from kernel layer when seq_len > 1024. suspect alignment assumptions in attention kernel.

sam: update to AcmeCorp: "We have applied a temporary routing fallback and are limiting parallel inference to reduce error rate. Expected customer impact reduced to <5% errors during mitigation window."

incident-bot: automated metric update: after fallback and concurrency change: error-rate dropped from 23% -> 6% in 3m. Eviction rate decreased.
leah: customer ack: AcmeCorp says they see improvements, but will reopen if they see regressions.

ravi: next steps: - collect nvcrash and kernel objdump from affected nodes - reproduce in staging with same seq_len distribution - open a CI job to fuzz attention kernel for misaligned pointers - prepare rollback patch for kernel memory ops.
marta: I’ll start repro in staging with identical batch/seq distribution. tagging @eng-ml for kernel review.
alice: thanks team. handing incident to postmortem owner: @marta. please start a timeline and root-cause notes. I’ll keep customer comms for high-severity tenants.
ops-bot: incident state: mitigation in-place, severity downgraded to P2 after error-rate stabilized.
incident-bot: summary logged -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/6234570001/summary
